newsitem.title: JAPAN: Iran raises September crude prices to Asia-traders.
newsitem.headline: Iran raises September crude prices to Asia-traders.

text.p: State-owned National Iranian Oil Co (NIOC) has lifted its September term crude price for Iran Light crude to Asia by 10 cents per barrel, traders said on Wednesday.
NIOC has raised the Asian term price for Iran Heavy by 20 cents, traders said.
This means that Iran Light crude oil for September loading will be priced at Oman's MPM minus 57 cents, with an automatic adjustment factor added to that.
The formula for Iran Heavy will be Dubai quotations minus 3 cents per barrel, with an automatic adjustment factor then subtracted.
The price of Iran Light is linked to Saudi Arabian Light crude, while Iran Heavy moves in tandem with Arabian medium crude.
Iranian crude prices are set on a quarterly basis.
However, under a contract agreement, NIOC and its customers can review prices whenever Saudi Arabian crude prices move substantially.

The adjustment factor used to calculate prices for both grades is defined as: 77 cents, minus the difference between Oman and Dubai, divided by two, or ((77 cts-(Oman-Dubai))/2. -- Tokyo Energy Desk +813-5473-3708
